objective: Close the three independent review findings exposed by public tauri_dialog: require a concrete detected instance before authorization, require confirmed absence after a decision, and omit provider-supplied surface references from public dialog metadata.
closed_decisions: Authorization is issued only when the immediately preceding detection retained a concrete private provider dialog instance; absence or uncertainty returns a bounded non-success result and issues no grant.

A supported provider decision is publicly verified only when the post-decision detection is the canonical confirmed-absent state: state unavailable, code provider_dialog_absent, and no retained dialog instance.
Provider-supplied surfaceRef remains available only for private binding checks and is omitted from all sanitized public dialog metadata; the runtime binding is authoritative.
Preserve explicit authorize=true, current binding checks, one-shot grant consumption, and the existing public tauri_dialog name/schema.
forbidden_changes: Do not edit files outside the four owned files.

Do not change public tool names or schema, provider routes, installer, vendored provider, packaging, process custody, dependencies, manifests, lockfiles, queue/blocker/release files, git, Jira, or pull requests.
Do not treat unsupported, unavailable-with-another-code, failed, malformed, or thrown postcondition checks as success.
Do not expose provider instance identifiers, grants, nonces, provider surface references, paths, raw causes, or expected/current binding values.

acceptance_criteria.description: Accept/cancel with authorize=true and no concrete detected dialog returns bounded non-success and neither issues nor consumes a grant nor calls the provider decision route.
After a supported decision, only explicit provider_dialog_absent is success; unsupported, failed, malformed, other unavailable codes, unchanged, or replaced dialogs produce bounded non-success.
Sanitized detection and decision metadata never contains provider-supplied surfaceRef or other private provider material, while private surface mismatch checks remain enforced.
Focused runtime/native-control tests and build pass, including regressions for all three findings.
